title: data_run_manifest.v1
description:
One run record per execution of one data-collection unit (audit units D01-D46), written by `nousergon_lib.run_manifest.run_unit` to `data_collection/runs/{unit_id}/{trading_day}/{run_id}.json`.

LIFTED from crucible's `run_manifest.v2` + `crucible.runner.run_job` on second adoption (`shared-code-policy` §2; `data_collection_plan_260914.md` §4.4). It is a SIBLING of that schema, not a copy of it: the collector's run is keyed by `unit_id` rather than by a crucible `job`, its outputs are S3 objects identified by ETag rather than store keys identified by content hash, and it carries the third status the collector genuinely has and crucible does not — `not_applicable`, for a unit whose cycle legitimately had nothing to do. Crucible's re-import onto this shared module is a tracked follow-up; until it lands, crucible keeps `run_manifest.v2` unchanged and this schema is the only implementation for the data component.

The rule the whole record exists for (`observability-policy` §3.1): the failure path writes the same telemetry as the success path, minus the completion claim. A dying run writes `status: failed` with its cause and never advances a downstream completion artifact.
$comment: Root stays OPEN per this package's additive-only contract rule (S3 Contract Safety): a new optional field may appear at any time, and removing or renaming a required one is a v2 with a dual-write window. The $defs rows below are closed, because each is a small fixed vocabulary whose growth is the schema change, not an accident of a producer.

schema_version.description: Const. A run record that cannot say which contract it was written under is unreadable by a consumer that has seen two versions.

run_id.description: The correlation identity (`observability-policy` §4): it appears on every log line, alert and cost row for this run. ULID — lexically sortable by creation time, so a listing of one unit's day is in execution order without parsing timestamps.

unit_id.description: The audit unit this run IS — `D01`..`D46`, optionally suffixed (`D15L`). The descriptor under `registry.d/units/` declaring this id also declares the `run_manifest_prefix` these records are written under, so the board's denominator and this record's address have one source.

trigger.description: How this execution was started. Closed: an unknown trigger is a run nobody can attribute, and `manual` exists precisely so a hand-run repair is counted as one rather than disguised as a schedule (`data_collection_plan_260914.md` §4.4).

trading_day.description: THE KEY. The NYSE trading day this run's work DESCRIBES, never the wall-clock date — a Saturday weekly run binds to Friday's close. It is half the manifest's own address.

calendar_date.description: The wall-clock UTC date the process actually ran. Distinct from `trading_day` on every weekend and holiday run; keeping both is what makes a backfill distinguishable from a same-day run.

status.description: Exhaustive, and deliberately WITHOUT a third `degraded`/`partial`/`unknown` state (crucible's rule, kept): `ok` means the unit produced its deliverable; `failed` means it did not, and pages. `not_applicable` is NOT a third success state — it is the answer for a cycle in which the unit was correctly asked to do nothing (a non-trading day; an upstream that declared no new data), it requires a reason from the closed list below, and it is COUNTED rather than silently skipped. A run that produced a partial or defective artifact is `failed`.

reason.description: Mandatory. Empty string when `status` is `ok`; an operator-readable cause when `failed`; one member of `not_applicable_reasons` when `not_applicable`. The conditionals below forbid an empty reason on the two non-ok statuses — a failure with no cause is indistinguishable from every other failure.

finished.description: RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix. Written on the failure path too — the manifest is written from a `finally`, so a dying run still records when it died.

code_sha.description: The 40-character commit sha of the tree that ran. Never a placeholder: a sha the process could not measure is a refusal at the start of the run, not a zero written at the end of it.

log_location.description: Where this run's FULL logs are, in the durable location the component declares (`observability-policy` §6.2) — the CloudWatch log group plus stream for a spot workload, the SSM log-capture key, or a local path for a laptop/CI run. Required, because a manifest that summarises a run without saying where to read it turns every diagnosis into a search.

inputs.description: Every artifact this run READ, by key and version. An empty list is legal and means the unit read nothing external.

outputs.description: Every artifact this run PUBLISHED, with the row count that landed in each. This is the field objective 6 is computed from — a manifest with `status: ok` and an output whose `rows_out` is 0 is the empty-but-fresh write, and it is countable here without opening the artifact.

rows_out.description: Records the unit published across all outputs. Kept at the top level as well as per-output so a unit with no single stable key (an ArcticDB append) still answers the question.

rows_rejected.description: Rejections WITH REASON, never a bare count. A count with no reason cannot be acted on, and is how 901 of 903 tickers silently failed a liquidity gate for months.

cost_usd.description: Spend attributable to this run. 0 is a real answer for a unit that spends nothing metered; it is required rather than optional so a fleet cost roll-up is computable rather than sampled from whichever runs happened to annotate it.

compute.description: `observability-policy` §3.3. Present on every manifest including laptop and CI runs, where `spot` is false and `instance_type` is `local`.

denominator.description: The declared population this run's coverage is measured against (`data_collection_plan_260914.md` §2 row 2) — the count, plus the key the count came from. Absent when the unit declares no denominator.

excluded.description: Symbols or records deliberately left out of the denominator, each with the declared exclusion class it was matched by. An undeclared missing record is a failure, never an exclusion — so an entry here is a citation of `contracts/exclusions/*.yaml`, not a free-text excuse.

guards.description: Every write-time guard that evaluated on this run and what it said — including the ones that passed, and including the ones running in observe mode whose verdict changed nothing. A guard that only records when it fires is indistinguishable from a guard that stopped running.

metrics.description: MetricRecord-shaped rows this run emitted, rendered onto the board. Open-shaped to match `krepis.metrics.MetricRecord`'s forward-compatible contract.

InputRef.description: One artifact this run read, identified by the version it was read AT — an ETag for an S3 object, a library/snapshot version for an ArcticDB read. Without a version an input reference cannot distinguish a rerun that read the same bytes from one that read different bytes at the same key.

OutputRef.description: One artifact this run published. `rows_out` is required — an output whose row count is unknown cannot be graded against a floor, and `null` is not permitted because 'we did not count' and 'we counted zero' are different facts with opposite consequences.

ComputeRow.description: What infrastructure this run consumed. `escalated_on_demand` is required so the fleet-wide spot-escalation rate is always computable (`cost-management-policy` §2.1).

instance_type.description: EC2 instance type, `lambda`, or `local` for a laptop or CI run.

GuardVerdict.description: One guard's reading. `mode` records whether the verdict had a consequence on this run, so an observe-mode period is legible after the fact rather than inferred from the absence of a failure (`sf-pipeline-policy` §7a).

verdict.description: `ok` passed; `empty_fresh` published an absent or empty artifact; `below_floor` published fewer rows than its declared floor; `unmeasurable` means the guard could not look — loud and red, never a pass; `not_applicable` means the unit declares no published key for this guard to grade.

not_applicable_reasons.description: The CLOSED list a `not_applicable` status draws its reason from. It grows only by PR, with the cycle that needed it named — a free-text reason is how a unit quietly stops being graded (`observability-policy` §3.5).
